memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: He stood between the living and the dead, and the plague stopped. But 14,700 people died from the plague, in addition to those who had died because of Korah. Then Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance to the tent of meeting, for the plague had stopped. — Num 16:48-50 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"He stood between the living and the dead, and the plague stopped." What a picture. Aaron, censer in hand, planted himself at the very boundary line between those still breathing and those who had fallen, and there the judgment halted. His intercession created a barrier that death could not cross. Behind him, the living were spared.

We should not overlook the cost: 14,700 people died. This is a sobering reminder that sin is deadly and its consequences real. Yet even amid the sorrow, the wonder is how many were saved. Without Aaron standing in the gap, the whole assembly might have perished. One faithful intercessor became the means of rescue for a multitude.

There is profound comfort here for us. We too live in a world under the shadow of sin and death. But we have a Priest who has stood between the living and the dead on our behalf — and He did not merely halt the plague for a time; He conquered death itself. Aaron's atonement stopped a plague for a day; Christ's atonement defeated death forever.

Jesus stands between us and the death our sin deserves. On the cross He took His place at that boundary line, and by His resurrection He broke through it, opening the way to everlasting life. Because He stands there, we who trust Him are on the side of the living. The plague of sin and death cannot reach us, for our great High Priest has stopped it with His own body and blood. What Aaron did for a moment, Christ has done for eternity. Stand behind Him, and live.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does it comfort you that Christ stands between you and death?
2. What does it mean that Aaron's momentary atonement points to Christ's eternal one?
3. How will you live today knowing you are on the side of the living in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Christ, my great High Priest, has stood between me and death and conquered it forever. Because He took His place at that boundary and rose again, I am on the side of the living. Let me live today in grateful, confident hope. Amen.
